items.title: UPDATE: Chamber extraordinary sitting, second reading of the refinery windfall tax. Budget committee backed the bill on 11 Nov without amendments; no sector/bank levy tabled so far
items.title_cs: AKTUALIZACE: Mimořádná schůze Sněmovny, 2. čtení daně na rafinerie; rozpočtový výbor 11. 11. návrh podpořil bez pozměňovacích návrhů
items.note: On 11 Nov the budget committee backed the government bill (50% rate, 2026–27, about CZK 5.5bn for 2026, in practice Orlen Unipetrol's Kralupy and Litvínov plants) and adopted no amendments. It rejected STAN's proposal to tax importers of foreign refinery output and STAN's proposal to limit the tax exemption on investment-flat sales. Papajanovský's (STAN) resolution asking the government not to add sector taxes through amendments failed. Amendments announced for the second reading: TOP 09/Jakob would cut the rate to 39.5% and remove deductibility from corporate income tax; the Pirates/Svobodová want 25% and extension to coal power producers. Sector taxes: Babiš told reporters on 11 Nov at Kbely that the government had not discussed them and 'Neočekávám ani, že by to proběhlo ve Sněmovně tento týden'. He is working on proposals with Schillerová but there is no coalition deal. Havlíček says the cabinet is not considering them now (ČTK 11 Nov: https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/babis-na-moznych-sektorovych-danich-pracuje-se-schillerovou/2900336). Okamura (SPD) says he will back no further taxes on citizens (5 Nov). Sitting time: NOT FOUND (psp.cz unreachable; Okamura called it as a single-item sitting, https://oenergetice.cz/energetika-v-cr/vlada-chce-zdanit-rafinerie-kvuli-vyssim-marzim-poslanci-chystaji-upravy). Third reading on Friday: no source mentions one; the sitting was called for the second reading only. OPEN: does the coalition table a sector or bank levy amendment on the floor despite Babiš's statement? Do the opposition amendments get filed? Is any third-reading date set?
